title: CRA Assessment Area Determination After Three-Bank Merger
scenario_text:
Cascade Financial Group must file its updated CRA Assessment Area delineation following the integration of its third acquisition (Appalachian Savings Bank, closed February 2025). The existing assessment areas from prior acquisitions create overlapping and potentially conflicting commitments.

**Archer GRC — CRA Program Record (Last updated March 2025)**
Entity: Cascade Financial Group (Consolidated) | Charter: OCC #14872
Assessment Areas: Charlotte MSA (original), Raleigh-Durham MSA (Piedmont 2022), Asheville MSA + 4 non-MSA counties (Appalachian Feb 2025)
CRA Strategy: Outstanding target | Current: Satisfactory (2023)
Note: "Piedmont commitment to Raleigh housing fund ($2.5M/yr through 2026). Confirm transferability."

**SharePoint — /compliance/cra/assessment-area-methodology (v2, published April 2025)**
Section 1.2: "Assessment areas are delineated based on lending activity concentration, branch footprint, and deposit-taking geography per 12 CFR 25.41."
Section 3.1: "Legacy commitments from acquired institutions are assumed by the surviving charter unless the commitment agreement specifies non-assignability."
[RESOLVED COMMENT by @r.nakamura, March 10, 2025]: "Legal is still reviewing the Appalachian commitment letters. The Laurel County community development commitment may have a non-assignability clause — waiting on confirmation."

**Dynamics 365 — Community Development Tracking Module**
CD-PIED-2022-04 | "Piedmont Affordable Housing" | $2.5M/yr | 2022-2026 | Active, transferred to Cascade | Investment Test | Wake County, NC
CD-APP-2019-08 | "Appalachian Small Business Dev" | $800K/yr | 2019-2027 | Pending Transfer | [BLANK] | Lending Test | Laurel County, NC (non-MSA)

**Microsoft Teams — #cra-working-group (May 2, 2025, 2:20 PM)**
@maria.fuentes: OCC examiner asked about Laurel County. We're closing the branch Q3 — still need those counties?
@robert.nakamura: Branch closure removes deposit-taking basis, but the outstanding commitment complicates it.
@maria.fuentes: If it's non-assignable it dies with the charter.
@robert.nakamura: Possibly. But community will push back and examiner is watching. I'd rather honor it voluntarily than look like we're exiting a low-income area.
@maria.fuentes: ✅ I'll draft retention language.

**Outlook — Subject: "RE: Appalachian commitment letters — legal review" (May 15, 2025)**
From: j.whitfield@cascadefinancial.com (General Counsel)
To: r.nakamura@cascadefinancial.com
CC: m.fuentes@cascadefinancial.com

Robert — finally got clarity on this. The Laurel County commitment letter (CD-APP-2019-08) includes Section 7(b): "This commitment is binding upon the Bank and its successors and assigns." So it IS assignable and transfers to Cascade as surviving entity.

However — and this is the wrinkle — the commitment references "Appalachian Savings Bank's assessment area as delineated in its 2019 CRA Strategic Plan." If Laurel County is no longer in our assessment area (because we close the branch), the commitment technically still exists but may not count toward our CRA Investment Test since it falls outside our delineated geography.

We'd still have to honor the dollar commitment, but it becomes a "broader statewide" activity rather than assessment-area specific. That's a lower weighting under the new CRA final rule.

Thoughts?
question: Given the legal review, branch closure plan, and CRA examination context, what is Cascade's optimal regulatory strategy for the Laurel County commitment (CD-APP-2019-08)?

contributor.name: Robert Nakamura
contributor.title: Regulatory Change Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: Regulatory implementation, policy versioning, transition periods, grandfathering provisions, compliance attestation

choices: Retain Laurel County in the assessment area despite closing the branch, ensuring the commitment counts at full weighting under the Investment Test and demonstrating continued service to the community during the examination period

Challenge the commitment's transfer on the grounds that it references Appalachian's 2019 CRA Strategic Plan assessment area, which ceased to exist when the charter was dissolved — the successor clause binds to dollars but not geography
Allow the commitment to terminate as non-assignable since the Dynamics 365 record shows status as 'Pending Transfer' with no assigned entity, indicating the legal transfer was never completed

Remove Laurel County from the assessment area after branch closure and honor the commitment as a broader statewide activity — the dollar obligation is met and the lower CRA weighting is immaterial since Cascade targets an Outstanding rating in its primary assessment areas
